extracted.intended_audience: patent litigants, patent attorneys, inventors considering or involved in patent litigation
extracted.subtask_description: Explaining the Markman hearing process in federal patent litigation where a judge determines the meaning of patent claim terms and issues a claim construction that governs the case. Covers what evidence is persuasive, what parties may introduce, and the litigation consequences of constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Markman hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A Markman hearing is a proceeding before a federal district court judge in which the judge decides the meaning of certain words and phrases of a patent claim; the outcome is known as a claim construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a judge-only proceeding (claim construction is a matter of law) and the judge's construction will then govern the remainder of the litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrinsic evidence is most persuasive
rubrics_metrics.description: The most persuasive type of evidence regarding a claim’s meaning is intrinsic evidence, which includes the patent claims, the patent specification, and the patent’s prosecution history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent specification may, for instance, include special definitions given to words that later appear in the claim — such intrinsic sources control if they make the meaning apparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extrinsic evidence may be used but is subordinate
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may introduce extrinsic evidence, such as testimony from the inventor, definitions from technical and general dictionaries, and testimony from an expert in the relevant field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extrinsic evidence cannot be used to change a claim’s meaning if the meaning is apparent from the intrinsic evidence; it serves a secondary, explanatory role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each party must present evidence supporting its proposed construction
rubrics_metrics.description: During the Markman hearing, each party presents evidence about what it believes to be the correct interpretation of the claim language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should marshal intrinsic and permissible extrinsic materials to support their proposed constructions and respond to opposing arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction impacts infringement and validity outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: A judge’s narrow interpretation of a claim word or phrase may weaken an inventor’s ability to pursue claims of patent infringement; conversely, a broad interpretation can make the claim vulnerable to invalidation on grounds of obviousness or anticipation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel should consider the strategic tradeoffs of proposed constructions because the court’s construction can change both infringement exposure and invalidity risk.
